{{Quote|Nice Deece. Ion pulse blaster, RPG anti-armor, ''and'' sniper?"''<br />''"Yeah. Full house.|A [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone trooper]] and clone commando [[Darman Skirata|Darman]]|<ref name="HC">''[[Republic Commando: Hard Contact]]''</ref>}}
The '''DC-17m Interchangeable Weapon System''' ('''DC-17m ICWS''') was a configurable combat weapons system used by the [[Clone commando/Legends|clone commandos]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. Designed by [[BlasTech Industries/Legends|BlasTech Industries]] to be able to meet the demands of the [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army of the Republic's]] elite [[Special forces/Legends|special forces]] [[Soldier/Legends|soldiers]], the DC-17m became the unique weapon of the Republic [[Commando/Legends|commandos]] throughout the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. An adaptable weapon, the DC-17m was capable of fulfilling multiple combat roles due to its ability to reconfigure into either a standard assault [[Blaster rifle/Legends|blaster rifle]], a compact [[Sniper rifle/Legends|sniper rifle]], or an anti-[[Armor/Legends|armor]] [[Grenade/Legends|grenade]] [[Grenade launcher/Legends|launcher]], depending upon the needs of the user. These traits made the DC-17m invaluable to its [[Cloning/Legends|clone]] commando owners, and the DC-17 proved a dangerous weapon against the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] on countless battlefields across [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], from the [[Desert/Legends|deserts]] of [[Geonosis/Legends|Geonosis]], to the [[City/Legends|cityscape]] of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], and the [[Tree/Legends|forests]] of [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]].

==Description==
{{Quote|Have a look through the Deece. Safety's on, but don't press anything.|Clone commando [[Atin Skirata|Atin]]|<ref name="HC" />}}
[[File:DC17mInterchangableWeaponSystem-FFp61.png|thumb|left|250px|A DC-17m ICWS components diagram]]
A product of [[BlasTech Industries/Legends|BlasTech Industries]],<ref name="GaW" /> the DC-17m Interchangeable Weapon System was a lighter and more versatile version of the [[DC-15]] [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] issued to the [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone trooper]] [[Infantry/Legends|infantry]] of the [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army of the Republic]]. Manufactured to a higher level of specification,<ref name="HC" /> the DC-17m's design ensured that it never jammed in the presence of excessive heat, cold, dust, or grime, though it required periodic calibration.<ref name="O66">''[[Order 66: A Republic Commando Novel]]''</ref> The DC-17m shared many of its internal parts and components with the smaller and similarly designated [[DC-17 hand blaster/Legends|DC-17 hand blaster]].<ref name="Guide to the Grand Army of the Republic">{{InsiderCite|84|Guide to the Grand Army of the Republic}}</ref> Unlike the [[Blaster pistol/Legends|blaster pistol]], the DC-17m was, at its root, a base stock which could be configured several different ways depending upon the needs of the user by way of numerous attachments: a standard [[Blaster rifle/Legends|blaster rifle]], a high-powered [[Sniper rifle/Legends|sniper rifle]], and an anti-[[Armor/Legends|armor]] [[Grenade launcher/Legends|grenade launcher]].<ref name="GaW" /> For the [[Clone commando/Legends|clone commandos]] for whom the rifle was standard issue and who trained with the DC-17m from a young age, changing the attachments was no more difficult than changing out a spent ammunition [[Blaster power pack/Legends|clip]],<ref name="O66" /> and they appreciated the reduction in load the DC-17 afforded them by combining three weapons on one platform.<ref name="GaW" /> The DC-17m stock was sturdy enough to be used as a [[Melee weapon/Legends|melee weapon]] in close combat, and the rifle had a safety setting to reduce misfires.<ref name="HC" /> Each DC-17m cost around 4500 [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]],<ref name="GaW" /> and [[Procurement Development|Republic Procurement]] was continuously seeking new add-ons for the weapon during the course of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]].<ref name="O66" />

===Blaster===
[[File:DC17m_rifle.jpg|thumb|right|250px|DC-17m with blaster rifle attachment]]
{{Quote|Which moron in Procurement ordered Deeces with the clip on the left? [...] Can't holster it right.''"<br />"''A moron who never had to fire it to save his life. Or thought that if you aimed right-handed, then your left was free to reach for a reload...|Clone commandos Corr and [[Niner Skirata|Niner]]|<ref name="O66" />}}
Perhaps the most often used attachment, the blaster rifle attachment, made the DC-17m a powerful, rapid-firing ion pulse assault rifle. Rather than Air cooling, the rifle uses coolant gas from side-loaded coolant clips, the DC-17m blaster could fire a maximum of sixty shots before requiring a coolant change; a [[Commando/Legends|commando's]] typical gear load included five coolant packs, for a total of three hundred rounds.<ref name="RepCom" />

The cross-trained commando, [[Corr Skirata|Corr]]—having served previously as a clone [[Trooper/Legends|trooper]] in [[Clone ordnance specialist/Legends|ordnance disposal]] prior to learning commando skills—found the left-mounted energy clip on the DC-17m's blaster to be a hindrance when holstering for beings that favored their right [[Limb/Legends|hand]]. First generation commandos that had been trained with the weapon since youth found no such complaint with the DC-17m, though they did note the oddity of the layout once the point was raised.<ref name="O66" />

===Sniper rifle===
[[File:DC17m_sniper2.jpg|thumb|right|250px|DC-17m with sniper rifle attachment]]
{{Quote|A well-built sniper rifle is a beautiful thing. Ours has two zoom modes, "Up close and personal" and "Hello, you're dead."|[[Sev/Legends|Sev]]|<ref name="RepCom">''[[Star Wars: Republic Commando]]''</ref>}}
The second attachment for the DC-17m allowed the blaster to convert into a long-range ion pulse [[Sniper/Legends|sniper]] rifle with an electromagnetic [[targeting scope]]. Coolant magazines for the sniper attachment carried five shots worth of coolant. The electromagnetic [[Scope/Legends|scope]] had two levels of zoom, adjusting the range between 10x and 20x magnification. The sights also provided an effect similar to an [[X-ray/Legends|x-ray]] at close range. A well-placed shot from the DC-17m's sniper attachment was known to be capable of [[Death/Legends|killing]] many types of enemies, from [[Droid/Legends|droids]] to several [[Species/Legends|species]] of organics. The sniper attachment was the preferred DC-17m configuration of the clone commandos [[Sev/Legends|Sev]]<ref name="RepCom" /> and [[Fi Skirata|Fi]],<ref name="HC" /> both of whom trained intensively as [[Clone sharpshooter/Legends|snipers]].<ref name="TZ" />

===Anti-armor===
[[File:DC17m_anti_armor.jpg|thumb|right|250px|DC-17m with anti-armor grenade attachment]]
{{Quote|Anti-Armor: Great against fortified droids, armored vehicles, and anyone else with an inflated opinion of himself.|[[Boss (clone commando)/Legends|Boss]]|<ref name="RepCom" />}}
A third configuration for the DC-17m was made possible by an attachment that transformed the rifle into an anti-armor [[Grenade launcher/Legends|grenade launcher]]. The launcher was loaded, one at a time, with dumb-fire grenades that could be launched several [[Foot/Legends|feet]] away from the user, and detonated on impact with any hard surface. Though the grenades were especially effective against heavily armored targets, the wide blast radius of the explosion made them good for damaging or destroying small enemy formations.<ref name="RepCom" /> Each grenade cost four hundred [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]],<ref name="GaW" /> and due to the size of the grenades, commandos typically carried only around four on their person. However, a number of individual [[Cloning/Legends|clones]] chose to equip their armor with additional holsters for carrying extra anti-armor rounds. One such clone was the [[Delta Squad/Legends|Delta Squad]] commando [[Scorch/Legends|Scorch]], who favored the explosive power of the grenade launcher attachment in battle.<ref name="RepCom" />

===Additional attachments===
{{Quote|Use the PEP laser and keep it nonlethal if you can.|[[Null-class Advanced Recon Commando|Null]] [[Advanced Recon Commando/Legends|ARC trooper]] [[Ordo Skirata|Ordo]]|<ref name="TZ" />}}
[[File:DC-17m_Interchangable_Weapon_System.jpg|thumb|left|200px|The DC-17m Interchangeable Weapon System with the [[DC-15s side arm blaster]]]]
By the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the second anniversary of the [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|Battle of Geonosis]], a fourth attachment to the DC-17m had been introduced to the Grand [[Army/Legends|Army's]] clone commandos: the non-lethal [[Pulsed energy projectile laser|Pulsed Energy Projectile]]—or "PEP"—laser. Originally a tool of [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] [[Law enforcement agency/Legends|law enforcement agencies]], the PEP [[Laser/Legends|laser]] was effective in riot and crowd control, or any other situation where death was undesirable. The weapon utilized a [[deuterium fluoride]] laser to stun targets into submission without inflicting permanent harm, although severe bruising and lingering pain were among potential side effects. The PEP laser attachment produced a powerful shockwave of both light and sound when it was discharged, and the impact from the device was described by one clone user as similar to being hit with a [[Flash grenade/Legends|flash-bang grenade]] and struck in the chest by several [[Plastoid/Legends|plastoid]] rounds at the same time.<ref name="TZ" />

In the [[19 BBY/Legends|third year]] of the Clone Wars, the [[Merr-Sonn Munitions, Inc./Legends|Merr-Sonn Munitions]] corporation released a fifth attachment for the DC-17m, this time a rapid-entry [[breaching grenade]]. While similar to the anti-armor attachment in many ways, the Merr-Sonn breaching grenade was specially designed to blow open sealed doors and [[hatch]]es from a safe distance, and was fired from a stand-off rod placed at the end of the DC-17's muzzle. The breaching grenade drew a few small criticisms from the [[Soldier/Legends|soldiers]] who used it: one clone commando stated that the stand-off rod made the DC-17 unwieldy and could potentially impair aiming, while another believed that it was too blunt of an instrument and an insult to their [[Standard year/Legends|years]] of elite training. In spite of these minor complaints, the attachment proved itself to be a useful tool in executing door breach maneuvers where a potentially dangerous and hostile force could be waiting on the other side.<ref name="TZ" />

==History==
{{Quote|Dar, give him a crash course in using a DC-17, will you?|[[Kal Skirata]] to clone commando Darman, referring to [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone trooper]] [[Corr Skirata|Corr]]|<ref name="TZ" />}}
The DC-17m Interchangeable Weapons System was one element of the standard issue equipment provided to all clone commandos in the Grand Army of the Republic's [[Special forces/Legends|special forces]] division, and their primary weapon in combat. Growing up on [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]], the clones were educated from a young age in how to utilize the advanced blaster rifle, first by [[Kaminoan/Legends|Kaminoan]] [[flash training]] simulation programs, then by the ''[[Cuy'val Dar]]'' [[Sergeant/Legends|sergeants]] recruited by [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]] to further train the commandos. Live-fire exercises in the [[clone military education complex]] of [[Tipoca City/Legends|Tipoca City]] honed the clones' skill with the DC-17m, and while each commando held their preference for the individual attachments and configurations, by the start of the Clone Wars, the commandos were capable of wielding the DC-17m blaster with incredible efficiency.<ref name="RepCom" /><ref name="HC" />

[[File:SevBossFixer.jpg|thumb|right|250px|DC-17m rifles in clone commando hands]]
As the weapon of choice for the Republic's clone commandos, the DC-17m made its mark on numerous fields of battle across the galaxy. On the [[Color/Legends|red]] [[Desert/Legends|desert]] plains of [[Geonosis/Legends|Geonosis]] during the war's first battle, ten thousand clone commandos brought their DC-17s against the [[Separatist Droid Army/Legends|forces]] of the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]].<ref name="TZ" /> Notably, the commandos of [[Delta Squad/Legends|Delta Squad]] wielded their rifles with deadly effectiveness in the destruction of a [[Geonosian/Legends|Geonosian]] [[Geonosis droid factories/Legends|droid foundry]] and a raid on a Confederacy [[Lucrehulk-class|''Lucrehulk''-class]] [[Core ship/Legends|Core Ship]].<ref name="RepCom" /> The DC-17m would further prove its worth on the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]]<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> [[Planet/Legends|world]] of [[Qiilura/Legends|Qiilura]], where the [[Omega Squad]]'s elite commandos destroyed a Confederacy [[Bioweapon/Legends|bioweapons]] facility and captured the CIS [[Scientist/Legends|scientist]], [[Ovolot Qail Uthan]].<ref name="HC" /> The DC-17m was used by [[Gregor/Legends|Gregor]], a captain in the [[212th Attack Battalion/Legends|212th Attack Battalion]] at the [[Battle of Sarrish/Legends|Battle of Sarrish]] where the Republic forces suffered a crushing defeat. Gregor survived the battle, but was listed as "Missing in Action" after suffering amnesia and finding himself on the Outer Rim planet [[Abafar/Legends|Abafar]] where he worked as a dishwasher. He was later discovered by the members of [[D-Squad/Legends|D-Squad]] who helped him recover his memory. Gregor then donned his old ''Katarn''-class armor and utilized his DC-17m rifle to help D-Squad escape the planet.<ref name="MIA">{{TCW|Missing in Action}}</ref>

[[File:GregorDC17m-FFp61.png|thumb|left|250px|Captain Gregor wielded his DC-17m rifle on Abafar.]]
The DC-17m enjoyed continued use during a Republic [[Raid on Fest|covert strike]] on the [[Water/Legends|snow]]-covered planet [[Fest/Legends|Fest]], a multi-[[Squad/Legends|squad]] undertaking to [[Mission to Coruscant (Clone Wars)|destroy]] a [[Jabiimi]] [[Terrorist/Legends|terrorist]] cell operating on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]],<ref name="TZ" /> the hunt for the rogue Kaminoan [[Clone Master/Legends|cloner]], [[Ko Sai/Legends|Ko Sai]],<ref name="Republic Commando: True Colors">''[[Republic Commando: True Colors]]''</ref> and the [[Battle of Haurgab|battle]] of [[Haurgab]]. Clone commandos relied on their DC-17m blasters during the [[Battle of Coruscant/Legends|attack]] on Coruscant orchestrated by [[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]], [[Supreme Commander of the Droid Armies/Legends|Supreme Commander of the Droid Armies]] of the Confederacy, late in the war. The specialized assault rifles were also instrumental to the commandos of [[Delta Squad/Legends|Delta Squad]] during their assigned [[Mission to Kashyyyk (Clone Wars)|mission]] to the [[Tree/Legends|arboreal]] [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of the Wookiees, [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]], and in the subsequent [[Battle of Kashyyyk/Legends|battle]] that erupted between the Confederacy and Republic shortly after.<ref name="O66" /> [[Ohnaka Gang/Legends|Hondo Ohnaka's pirates]] also made use of these weapons.

After the [[Declaration of a New Order|transformation]] of the Galactic Republic into the new [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], the clone commandos that had formerly served in the Republic Grand Army's [[Special Operations Brigade/Legends|Special Operations Brigade]] were reassigned to the [[Imperial Commando Special Unit]]—a new special operations division within the [[Imperial Army/Legends|Imperial Army's]] [[501st Legion/Legends|501st Legion]], under the [[Commander/Legends|command]] of [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]]. Despite the changes to their serial numbers, their armor, and the names of their squads, the commandos were allowed the retention of their DC-17m rifles. Commandos from Imperial [[Squad 40]] used their DC-17s in a [[Mission to Celen|confrontation]] with former [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Iri Camas]], and to [[Mission to Coth Fuuras space station|hunt down]] the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Borik Yelgo]], missions that both ended with the targets' death.<ref name="ImpCom" />

==Behind the scenes==
The DC-17m Interchangeable Weapons System first appeared in the [[2004]] novel ''[[Republic Commando: Hard Contact]]'', by [[Author/Legends|author]] [[Karen Traviss]] as a tie-in to the subsequent [[2005]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: Republic Commando]]'', for which the weapon was created and prominently featured. The DC-17, as the blaster used by all the clone commandos, went on to appear in every novel in the [[Republic Commando|''Republic'' and ''Imperial Commando'' series]]. The [[2008]] reference book ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'' featured a brief informational entry for the DC-17m.
